figures.label: 圖一
figures.caption: 圖一：櫃台前排隊點餐
figures.description: 一家速食店的櫃台前，五名顧客排成一列等候點餐。櫃台後有兩名戴帽子的店員：一人看著收銀機替顧客點餐，另一人把裝好餐點的托盤遞給排在最前面的顧客。櫃台上方掛著菜單看板。隊伍最後面的一名學生低頭看手錶，看起來有點著急。

figures.label: 圖二
figures.caption: 圖二：在自助點餐機前操作
figures.description: 同一家速食店改裝後，櫃台前排著三台直立式自助點餐機，螢幕上有漢堡、飲料的圖示與「付款」按鈕。兩名年輕人各站在一台機器前，用手指點選螢幕，很快就拿到號碼單。最右邊的機器前站著一位白髮的長者，一手拿著老花眼鏡，皺著眉頭盯著螢幕，頭上畫著幾個問號；他身後等候的人越排越長。櫃台只剩一名店員在出餐口叫號。

questions.stem: 提示：近年來，不少速食店在店內設置自助點餐機，讓顧客自己在螢幕上點餐、付款，櫃台的點餐人員也隨之減少。請仔細比較下列兩張圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段比較圖一與圖二兩種點餐方式有何不同；第二段說明你對以自助點餐機取代人工點餐的看法，並以你自己或家人的經驗支持你的看法。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有三個要求：第一段比較兩張圖的點餐方式；第二段表明你對「點餐機取代店員」的看法，並用自己或家人的經驗支持。第二段只寫「點餐機很方便」或「很不方便」都太單薄，要說清楚是誰、在哪裡、發生了什麼事，再說這件事如何影響你的看法。
evidence: 第一段比較圖一與圖二兩種點餐方式有何不同
並以你自己或家人的經驗支持你的看法
1.strategy_zh: 先列出兩張圖的三組對比（誰服務、速度、誰覺得困難），第二段的立場要和經驗互相呼應，不要經驗講方便、結論卻說反對。
hints: 第一段：先寫圖一的排隊與店員服務，再用轉折語帶出圖二的不同
別漏掉圖二那位長者：他是第二段看法的伏筆
第二段：立場一句、經驗兩三句、理由與結論各一句

moves.zh: 比較圖一與圖二兩種點餐方式有何不同
說明你對以自助點餐機取代人工點餐的看法
以你自己或家人的經驗支持你的看法

content.focus_zh: 第一段要同時寫出兩張圖的差異（排隊等候、店員服務 vs. 自己點選、速度較快），並注意圖二那位不知所措的長者；第二段要有明確立場（贊成、反對或有條件贊成），再用自己或家人的一次具體經驗撐住看法。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。

空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段宜用「圖一…；相較之下，圖二…」的對照架構；第二段先表態，再接經驗與理由，最後回扣題目，兩段之間要用轉承語銜接。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在式或現在進行式，敘述經驗改用過去式；比較句（faster than、while、whereas）與被動語態（has been replaced by）要寫對。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 點餐相關用語（order、counter、cashier、screen、self-ordering machine）要用得準確，避免整篇只用 machine 與 good、bad 這類籠統字。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The two pictures show two different ways of ordering food at a fast-food restaurant. In the first picture, five customers are standing in line in front of the counter. Two workers are taking orders and handing out trays, so each customer has to wait for a turn. In the second picture, however, the cashiers have been replaced by three self-ordering machines. Two young people are touching the screens and getting their numbers quickly. On the other hand, an old man is staring at the screen with a confused look, and the line behind him is getting longer.
In my opinion, self-ordering machines are helpful, but they should not completely replace cashiers. First, the machines save time, especially for young people who are used to using phones. However, not everyone can use them easily. For example, last winter I took my grandmother to a fast-food restaurant near our home. She wanted to order a burger by herself, but the small words on the screen made her nervous. In the end, she asked me to order for her and looked a little embarrassed. Because of this experience, I believe restaurants should keep at least one cashier for customers who need help. In short, machines can make ordering faster, but a friendly worker is still important.

paragraphs.function_zh: 比較兩張圖：櫃台排隊點餐與自助點餐機的差別，並點出長者的困難
paragraphs.topic_sentence: The two pictures show two different ways of ordering food at a fast-food restaurant.

paragraphs.function_zh: 看法＋經驗：有條件贊成，用陪奶奶點餐的經驗說明為什麼要保留店員
paragraphs.topic_sentence: In my opinion, self-ordering machines are helpful, but they should not completely replace cashiers.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
The two pictures capture how ordering at a fast-food restaurant has changed in recent years. In the first scene, five customers are lined up at the counter, where two staff members are busy taking orders and handing a loaded tray to the customer at the front. The process looks slow but personal, since every customer gets to speak to a real person. The second scene, by contrast, is dominated by three tall self-ordering kiosks. Two young customers are tapping through the menu in seconds, while only one worker remains behind the counter to call out order numbers. Yet the most striking figure stands at the last machine: an elderly man holding his reading glasses, frowning at the screen as if it were written in a foreign language. Behind him, the line keeps growing, making him look even more overwhelmed.
Personally, I welcome the kiosks, but I do not think they should replace cashiers entirely. Admittedly, some degree of automation is inevitable, and the machines bring clear benefits: they cut waiting time, reduce mistakes in orders, and help restaurants save on labor costs. However, efficiency should not come at the expense of the customers who are left behind, especially older people who find touch screens intimidating. My grandfather is a case in point. Last summer, he tried to buy breakfast at a fast-food restaurant on his own, only to find that the counter had no cashier at all. After pressing the wrong button three times, he gave up and went home hungry. When he told me about it, he laughed, yet I could hear the embarrassment in his voice. What troubled me most was not the machine itself but the message it seemed to send: customers like him no longer belonged there. Therefore, I believe every restaurant should keep at least one staffed counter or assign a worker to guide customers at the kiosks during busy hours. After all, hospitality is not only about speed; a good restaurant should make every customer, young or old, feel welcome.

paragraphs.function_zh: 比較兩張圖：從「慢但有人情味」到「快卻有人跟不上」，用長者這個細節收尾
paragraphs.topic_sentence: The two pictures capture how ordering at a fast-food restaurant has changed in recent years.

paragraphs.function_zh: 看法＋經驗：先讓步承認點餐機的好處，再用爺爺的經驗說明效率不能犧牲被落下的人，最後提出具體做法與見解
paragraphs.topic_sentence: Personally, I welcome the kiosks, but I do not think they should replace cashiers entirely.

errors.explanation_zh: small words 在英文多指「短字、簡單的字」，用來表達「螢幕上字很小」是中文「小字」的直譯，用字不精準。
errors.suggestion: the tiny text on the screen／the small print on the screen

steady.comment_zh: 第一段對照兩圖（排隊等候與店員服務 vs. 自己點選、拿號碼快，並寫到不知所措的長者），第二段先表態「有用但不應完全取代」，再用帶外婆點餐的經驗支持，回應三項要求。文法正確，完成式被動 have been replaced by 用得好；但 the small words on the screen 是中文「小字」的直譯，字彙上 machines 重複多次、整體偏基本。

top.comment_zh: 第一段以 by contrast 對照兩圖，連店員人數、長者拿老花眼鏡、身後隊伍變長都寫到；第二段立場明確（歡迎但不應全面取代），先讓步列出好處，再以祖父自己點餐失敗、餓著回家的經驗撐住論點，最後提出保留人工櫃台或引導人員的具體建議並回扣 hospitality。句型（as if it were、only to find、What troubled me most was…）與字彙（kiosks、automation、intimidating、a case in point）都很成熟，無語言錯誤。

status_reason: blind_solver:A 未通過：E1（穩健版） 有 1 個語言錯誤（範文要 0 錯，出題規格書 WRT-MOD-ERR-01）：the small words on the screen；判定者（第 1 輪）：同意退回。穩健版第二段 the small words on the screen 是中文「小字」的直譯（英文 small words 通常指「短字」），應改成 the small print／the tiny text on the screen；盲評 B 也指出這個搭配不道地。題目與頂標版範文沒有問題，修改穩健版這一句後重新盲評即可
